'''Miwa Shrine''' (美和神社, *Miwa Jinja*) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in Miyamoto-chō, Kiryu City, Gunma Prefecture, Japan. It is listed as a minor {{ill|2=ja|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/2=ja|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} and was formerly Ranked as a {{ill|2=ja|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|qid=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|qid=Q90139226|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/2=ja|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to JA}} under the old shrine Ranking system.

==Overview==
Miwa Shrine enshrines {{ill|2=ja|Ōmononushi Kushi-mika-tama-no-Mikoto|ja|大物主櫛甕玉命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/2=ja|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to JA}} ({{ill|Ōmononushi|en|Ōmononushi|qid=Q10936701|qid=Q10936701|lt=Ōmononushi|1=Ōmononushi}}) and {{ill|2=ja|Takehayasusanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|武速須佐之男命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/2=ja|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to JA}} ({{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|en|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qid=Q272993|lt=Susanoo-no-Mikoto|1=Susanoo-no-Mikoto}}). It is situated at the southeastern foot of Mount Agatsuma in Kiryu, facing Yamate-dori Avenue. The shrine is known for hosting performances of {{ill|Kagura|en|Kagura|qid=Q1348260|lt=Kagura|1=Kagura}} and taiko drumming during the annual {{ill|2=ja|Kiryu Ebisu Festival|ja|桐生ゑびす講|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/2=ja|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to JA|1=Kiryū Nishinomiya Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11537354}} held from November 19–20. A mikoshi (portable shrine) storehouse for the {{ill|2=ja|Kiryu Yagibushi Festival|ja|桐生八木節まつり|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/2=ja|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to JA|1=Kiryū Yagibushi festival|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11537271}} is located adjacent to the worship hall.

==History==
Miwa Shrine is traditionally said to have been established during the reign of Emperor Sujin, the 10th emperor of Japan, with its deity transferred from Mount Miwa in Yamato Province. It was officially recognized as a shrine in 796 (Enryaku 15) alongside {{ill|Kamo shrines|en|Kamo shrines|qid=Q1306606|lt=Kamo Shrine|1=Kamo shrines}} (as recorded in the {{ill|Nihon Kōki|en|Nihon Kōki|qid=Q1077029|lt=Nihon Kōki|1=Nihon Kōki}}). In 880 (Gangyō 4), it was awarded the Rank of Senior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade, alongside other shrines such as {{ill|Kamo shrines|en|Kamo shrines|qid=Q1306606|lt=Kamo Shrine|1=Kamo shrines}}, {{ill|2=ja|Kohachisu Shrine|ja|甲波宿禰社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/2=ja|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to JA}}, and {{ill|2=ja|Oiwai Shrine|ja|小祝社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/2=ja|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to JA}}, as documented in the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|en|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|qid=Q1052981|qid=Q1052981|lt=Sandai Jitsuroku|1=Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku}}.

The shrine was referred to as "Conferred First Rank Miwa Daimyōjin" in the {{ill|2=ja|Kōzuke no Kuni Jinmyōchō|ja|上野国神名帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/2=ja|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to JA}}. Unfortunately, it lost many of its historical records and treasures in a fire during the Tenshō era.

Miwa Shrine was originally affiliated with {{ill|2=ja|Enman-ji Temple|ja|円満寺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/2=ja|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to JA}} ({{ill|Enmanji (Kiryu)|ja|円満寺 (桐生市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Enmanji (Kiryu)|1=Enman-ji Temple|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11394812}}), and both were managed by the Kojima family during the Edo period. It was designated as a Gōsha in 1872 (Meiji 5) and merged with the former {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|en|Yasaka Shrine|qid=Q692714|lt=Yasaka Shrine|1=Yasaka Shrine}} of Honmachi 3-chome in 1908 (Meiji 41).

==Sub-Shrines==
* '''Yasaka Shrine''' – Former Village shrine, merged in 1908
* '''Yagokoro-omoikane Shrine''' – Former precinct shrine of Yasaka Shrine
* '''Hata Shrine''' – Former precinct shrine of Yasaka Shrine
* '''Ichigami Shrine (Horinwa Gongen)''' – Former precinct shrine of Yasaka Shrine
* '''Matsuo Shrine'''
* '''Kotohira Shrine'''
* '''Nishinomiya Shrine'''
